column1:
The FOMC’s December 2018 statement signals a strong current economy (solid job gains, low unemployment, robust household spending) and inflation near its symmetric 2% objective, coupled with a 25 bp rate hike to a 2.25–2.50% target range (IOER at 2.40%) and continued balance-sheet runoff. Interpreted through the literature: (1) With longer-term inflation expectations “little changed,” gradual tightening is consistent with inflation-forecast targeting and adherence to the Taylor principle, helping anchor inflation around target. (2) Emphasis on credibility and a symmetric 2% goal addresses the inflation-bias issue under discretion and aligns with the Friedman–Phelps view of no long-run unemployment–inflation trade-off. (3) Noting that business fixed investment has moderated accords with macro-finance evidence that higher real rates and tighter financial conditions temper investment and near-term output.

Adjustment using the FSR lens: The Financial Stability Report around this time highlighted elevated asset valuations, rising nonfinancial business leverage (including leveraged loans with weakening underwriting), and potential vulnerabilities from a sharp tightening in financial conditions, even as banks and core funding markets appeared resilient. Against this backdrop, the FOMC’s signal of “some further gradual increases” and continued balance-sheet runoff suggests a more cautious forward-looking stance than the statement alone implies, given the system’s sensitivity to risk sentiment and credit conditions.

Net assessment: Positive on current conditions but tempered by identified financial stability vulnerabilities and tighter financial conditions risk; forward-looking tone is moderately positive but less upbeat than before.
